sections.h2: Where is Wayne County, Indiana, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Wayne County is in east central Indiana on the Ohio border, and Richmond is its county seat and largest city. The county was formed in 1811 and named for Gen. Anthony Wayne. Its seat was first Salisbury, moved to Centerville in 1818 and settled in Richmond in 1873.

The county covers about 404 square miles. Randolph County lies to the north, Darke and Preble counties in Ohio to the east, Union County to the south, Fayette to the southwest and Henry to the west. Hoosier Hill, the highest natural point in Indiana at 1,257 feet, is in the county.

Smaller places in the county include Centerville, Cambridge City and Hagerstown, plus Dalton, Pennville and Fountain City. Richmond covers about 24 square miles and held 35,720 people in the 2020 census.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about homes in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Wayne County has a median owner-occupied home value of $140,200 and an owner-occupancy rate of 69.2%. The Census Bureau estimates 66,169 residents as of July 1, 2025, down 0.6% from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What drives the Wayne County economy?
sections.html:
Health care, retail and manufacturing history shape Wayne County's economy. The Census Bureau counted 1,453 employer establishments and 25,774 jobs in 2023, and health care and social assistance receipts reached about $1.08 billion in 2022.

  • Retail sales were about $1.28 billion in 2022.
  • Accommodation and food services sales were about $170 million.
  • Richmond has four colleges: Earlham College, Indiana University East, Ivy Tech and Purdue Polytechnic.
  • The city was once called the lawnmower capital, and Wayne Works built school buses until 1992.

Median household income is $55,692, and 18.3% of residents are in poverty. About 20.5% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and the average commute is 21.8 minutes.

sections.h2: How do roads, history and climate shape Wayne County homes?
sections.html:
Richmond is served by Interstate 70 at exits 149, 151, 153 and 156, and US 40, the old National Road, passes through the city. The nearest commercial airport is Dayton International, and Roseview Transit, owned by the city, runs daily except Sundays and major holidays.

Richmond was settled by Quaker families in 1806 and incorporated as a city in 1840. Its historic districts include Downtown, Old Richmond, Starr and the Depot area, and five large districts are listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Older houses in those areas often need more upkeep than newer ones.

Climate data for Richmond show a January average low of 15 degrees and a July average high of 85. Monthly precipitation runs from 2.27 inches in February to 4.41 inches in May, and the record low is minus 29 degrees, set in January 1994. Roofs, furnaces and foundations take the brunt of that range, and repair needs are a common reason owners consider selling as-is.

sections.h2: How does the Wayne County Assessor value property and handle appeals?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Assessor values each parcel, and the Assessor's office is on the lower level of the Wayne County Administration Building at 301 E. Main St. in Richmond. Tim Smith was the assessor in 2025. The assessed value of any parcel can be looked up on Beacon, the Schneider online records site.

Wayne County is in the 2022 to 2025 reassessment cycle. The state's ratio study narrative says townships reviewed in the latest phase were Clay, Franklin, New Garden, Webster and the northeast quadrant of Wayne Township, with a target of 25% of parcels reviewed. It also groups the county into Center Township, a small-town hub near Centerville, Wayne Township, which contains Richmond, and the remaining rural townships.

Indiana's general appeal rule uses Form 130:

  • File by June 15 of the year that matches your notice. In 2025 the Wayne deadline reported by local news was June 16.
  • File one petition per parcel.
  • The PTABOA must hold a hearing within 180 days.
  • Appeal a PTABOA decision to the Indiana Board of Tax Review with Form 131.

We could not confirm the 2026 Wayne deadline from an official page, so check the date on your notice.

sections.h2: What happened with Wayne County assessments in 2025?
sections.html:
Wayne County's average assessment rose 15% in 2025, according to Western Wayne News. Assessor Tim Smith said the state raised its cost tables 30 to 35% across the board because of labor and material costs, and that 2024 assessments for sold properties averaged about 78% of sale prices.

Form 11 notices had to be mailed by April 30. Owners could scan the QR code on the notice to appeal online, download Form 130, or go to the assessor's office. Smith said an appeal leads to an individual review of the property rather than the mass assessment.

A seller who got a large increase should keep that notice. A higher assessment can carry over into a buyer's costs, and an appeal that is still open at closing is worth mentioning to the title company.

sections.h2: When are Wayne County property taxes due and how do you pay?
sections.html:
Wayne County property tax is due May 11 and November 10 in 2026, and the treasurer mails one bill a year by April 15 with both coupons. Penalties begin the day after each due date, and partial payments are accepted any time, though the full amount is due by the deadline.

InstallmentDue5% penalty from10% penalty from
SpringMay 11, 2026May 12June 11
FallNovember 10, 2026November 11December 10

A 10% penalty applies instead of 5% if the owner has prior delinquent taxes. The treasurer is Beth Fields, at 401 East Main Street, second floor of the Wayne County Annex, phone (765) 973-9238. Hours are Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30.

  • Online at taxes.quickviewhere.com, using the access code on your bill. Online balances do not include penalties, so call for the amount owed after the due date.
  • By phone at 1-877-690-3729, jurisdiction code 2412. Card fees apply.
  • By mail or in the drop box at the Annex. No cash in the box.
  • In person at participating banks from April 14 to May 11, 2026, for a fee of $1 or $2 per parcel depending on the bank.

sections.h2: What if you sell a Wayne County house with delinquent tax?
sections.html:
You can sell with delinquent tax, because the title company pays it from your proceeds. Tax sale information for Wayne County runs through sriservices.com, and questions about redeeming a parcel after a sale go to the County Auditor.

Before you sell, call the treasurer for the exact amount including penalties, since the online balance leaves them out. Then compare that number with the price you expect to net.

We buy houses in Wayne County as-is, including ones with back taxes, repairs or tenants. The offer is ours to make and yours to decline, and nothing is owed if you say no.

faqs.q: When are Wayne County, Indiana property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due May 11 and November 10 in 2026. The treasurer mails one bill by April 15 that has both installments.

faqs.q: What are the penalties in Wayne County?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5% from the day after the due date and 10% after about 30 days. It is 10% from the start if you have prior delinquent taxes.

faqs.q: Where is the Wayne County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The office is at 401 East Main Street in Richmond, on the second floor of the Annex Building. The phone is (765) 973-9238.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Wayne County assessment?
faqs.a: File Indiana Form 130 with the Assessor, one per parcel, by June 15 of the right year. In 2025 the reported Wayne deadline was June 16.

faqs.q: Can I check my Wayne County assessed value online?
faqs.a: Yes. The treasurer's page points owners to the Beacon site, where assessed values can be looked up.
